Historical coupling and identification synthesis.

# Question

For aqueous monoethanolamine (MEA) and CO₂, can the carbamate/bicarbonate split
separately identify reaction constants from ionic Born/dispersion and dielectric
effects under the exact model and data domain?

# Result

Independent identification is not established. The historical reaction-temperature fit retained all five reactions and two singular-value-decomposition (SVD)
directions. Those two directions reduce fitting freedom; they are not the two
net reactions. This distinction prevents a numerical rank statement from being
mistaken for a chemical species reduction.

# Basis and method

[]{#chemical-coupling}

The six-species comparison derives carbamate formation as CO₂ hydration (R2) − carbamate hydrolysis (R4) − MEAH⁺ dissociation (R5) and
bicarbonate formation as R2 − R5. Their log equilibrium constants differ by
−ln K₄, the negative log equilibrium constant of carbamate hydrolysis. Both net reactions share MEA, CO₂ and MEAH⁺, so carbon, amine and
charge balances couple their amounts. Activity coefficients also change with
the shared mixture composition.

# Values

[]{#what-has-been-tested}

The staged work already tested neutral binary vapor–liquid equilibrium (VLE), historical ionic/speciation parameter
regression, bounded CO₂/R4 calibration, dielectric formulations, reaction
temperature directions and paired heat. The [volumetric source inventory](https://github.com/tannerpolley/Amine-Thermodynamics/blob/4822946494a9c48f2fcbb02f9b3f9627077c1fe5/docs/ePC-SAFT/meah-meacoo-volumetric-evidence.md)
keeps analog densities, bulk MEA densities and derived volumes separate. It found no numerical exact aqueous MEAH⁺/MEACOO⁻ salt-density
evidence in the bounded search.

The July coupled designs specified joint pressure/speciation objectives,
frozen bounds, grouped partitions, multistart and identification requirements.
The 28 July shared-ion fit converged but worsened pressure; the August
pressure-first screen did not resolve the fit; Issue 70 retained a supported
negative decision. These results make the estimation strategy established
work, not an unresearched gap.

# Limits and evidence type

[]{#remaining-identification-boundary}

The historical [reaction-temperature fit](../reaction-temperature-fit/index.qmd)
held equation-of-state (EOS) parameters fixed and barely changed paired speciation error. The earlier ionic fit was not a joint identification study
of the current selection.

This is a synthesis of historical calibration and diagnostic evidence; it is not an independent identification or physical-validation study.

# Records

::: {.callout-note}
This page connects retained analyses. It does not introduce a new parameter regression or
replace the exact calculation records linked below.
:::

Before another fit, reconcile the reviewed evaluator correction and owner-held
formation/partition reaction-intercept sensitivity results (F/S) and ionic-screen results in the [scientific context map](https://github.com/tannerpolley/Amine-Thermodynamics/blob/codex/born-permittivity-formulation-study/docs/scientific/docs/scientific/CONTEXT.md)
and [September audit](https://github.com/tannerpolley/Amine-Thermodynamics/blob/codex/born-permittivity-formulation-study/docs/scientific/REPOSITORY_AUDIT_2026-09-08.md).
Do not treat a successful solve, a historical fit vector or a two-dimensional
sensitivity subspace as evidence of independent parameter identification.
